solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable copy, its numbering matching the numbers printed in it and the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: An act of contrition involving mostly chaste time, conveying legal right

indicators.note: a thing involving others takes them inside itself, so one part goes within another

parts.note: the indefinite article as a single letter
penance is an act done to show sorrow for sin

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: chaste means pure; mostly leaves off its last letter
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone performs a penance, keeping chaste for a while, and somehow gains a legal right.
explanation.walkthrough: An act of contrition looks like the definition, but it is wordplay; the legal sense sits at the end of the clue, a right that goes with property when it is conveyed.
explanation.definitionFit: In law an appurtenance is a minor right or property attached to a holding, which passes along with it when the land is conveyed.

clue.text: Component of uric acid in pee-pee

parts.note: pee is the spoken name of the letter P
pee in its everyday sense is urine

explanation.surface: A chemistry note on what is found in children's wee.
explanation.walkthrough: The childish doubling 'pee-pee' is split: the first 'pee' is the letter's name, the second its bodily sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Uric acid is chemically a purine derivative, so a purine is a structural building block of that compound.

clue.text: High-pitched sound from line dressed for hunting?

indicators.note: to be dressed in something is to be wrapped by it, so one letter goes inside the clothing word

parts.note: hunting pink is the scarlet coat worn by foxhunters
L is the usual abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A huntsman's outfit apparently makes a tinny noise.
explanation.walkthrough: Hunting pink is the red coat of the British foxhunt, despite its colour being scarlet; L dressed in it gives P(L)INK.
explanation.definitionFit: A plink is a short, sharp, high metallic note, like a plucked string or a tap on glass.

clue.text: Extinct sea creature, form of thin ray

indicators.note: a form of something is that thing remade in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A naturalist suggests a lost sea beast was just a skinny type of ray.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhytina is the genus name of Steller's sea cow, a huge marine mammal hunted to extinction in the 18th century.

clue.text: Herbal infusion from one of the cordylines, healthy

parts.note: the ti, or cabbage tree, is a palm-like plant of the genus Cordyline
sane means sound or healthy, especially in mind

explanation.surface: A health-food claim that a soothing tea is brewed from a garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tisane is a tea made by steeping herbs or flowers rather than tea leaves.

clue.text: Nasty water spirit that is going after a duck

indicators.note: going after puts one part behind the other in reading order

parts.note: nix means nothing, and a duck is a score of nothing in cricket
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A malevolent sprite is pictured chasing a duck across a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: The duck is not a bird but a zero score, as in cricket, so it means nothing: NIX.
explanation.definitionFit: In Germanic folklore a nixie is a malicious female water sprite that lures people to drown.

clue.text: Dad's up and down? That's obvious

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Dad is PA, read upwards
Dad read the normal way down is a parent

explanation.surface: A father who is either up or down is plainly visible, or so the remark goes.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad serves twice: as PA read upwards, then as PARENT read the normal way, down the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent means clearly visible or plain to see, a straightforward synonym of obvious.

clue.text: Something to go with tattie? If I cooked with it, that'll make fine pie

indicators.note: cooked means altered or doctored, so letters are mixed together into a new order
the answer plus some letters will make the phrase, so those added letters are taken away to leave it

parts.note: the full set of letters the mixture produces
these letters are subtracted from the set

explanation.surface: A cook boasts that adding a vegetable to the potato will produce a fine pie.
explanation.walkthrough: A compositional anagram: the answer with IF I, rearranged, gives FINE PIE. Neeps and tatties are turnips and potatoes, the Scottish side dish served with haggis.
explanation.definitionFit: Neep is Scots for a turnip or swede, the traditional partner of tatties, potatoes, with haggis.

clue.text: Paddy, for example, like McCoy after Church?

indicators.note: after places the second part behind the first in reading order

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
the real McCoy is the genuine article

explanation.surface: Paddy sounds like an Irishman named McCoy heading out of church.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddy looks like an Irish name, but it is a paddy field, where rice grows.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddy is a rice field and also rice itself in the husk, and rice is a cereal grain.

clue.text: Irish rustic church I concealed in devious clue

indicators.note: something concealed in another is hidden inside it, so two letters sit within the others
devious means twisting and indirect, so the letters wander out of order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
CH is the standard abbreviation for church
taken as written

explanation.surface: A setter hides a reference to a country chapel inside a tricky clue.
explanation.walkthrough: CH and I go into CULE, the rearranged CLUE: CUL(CHI)E.
explanation.definitionFit: Culchie is Irish slang, often mildly scornful, for a country person from outside Dublin.

clue.text: Strong wind coated crop in tatters (10, two words)

indicators.note: something in tatters is torn to shreds, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gale has left a farmer's covered harvest ripped to shreds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cape Doctor is the strong dry south-easterly that blows over Cape Town, said to clear away pollution.

clue.text: Teds err wandering round etc — what urban youth aspires to? (10, two words)

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so one set of letters wraps another
wandering letters stray from their places and end up in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Teddy boys go astray chasing the respect every young city kid wants.
explanation.walkthrough: Teds are Teddy boys, 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style dress; the rearranged letters surround etc.
explanation.definitionFit: Street cred is credibility with fashionable young people, the standing in urban culture that young city dwellers seek.

clue.text: Regular refrain from nurse about runs

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps around a letter

parts.note: an aia, or ayah, is a nursemaid in India
R is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A nurse hums the same tune again and again on her rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The nurse is an Indian nursemaid, spelt aia or ayah in Chambers; runs is the cricket scorer's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in opera, often with a recurring air, so it serves as a refrain.

clue.text: Comfort e.g. for each in part of Divine Office

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another word

parts.note: Sext is the canonical hour said at midday
per means for each, as in miles per hour

explanation.surface: A cleric seeks comfort in each of the daily prayer services.
explanation.walkthrough: Comfort is a person, not a feeling: Alex Comfort, author of The Joy of Sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Alex Comfort, author of The Joy of Sex, is a famous example of a jokey expert on sex.

clue.text: I'm regularly smashed at Christmas — one should be into some milk?

indicators.note: one thing being into another means it sits inside it

parts.note: a pinta is British slang for a pint of milk
a means one

explanation.surface: A drinker confesses to getting drunk every Christmas and wonders if one should switch to milk.
explanation.walkthrough: Smashed suggests drunk, but it is literal: the answer is beaten open. A goes into PINTA, from the 1950s ad slogan 'Drinka pinta milka day': PIN(A)TA.
explanation.definitionFit: A piñata is a decorated container of sweets that children break open with sticks at festive parties, including Christmas in Mexico.

clue.text: Like former debt given back, it's often disposable these days

indicators.note: given back means returned, so the word runs the other way

parts.note: a debt that is in the past has been repaid

explanation.surface: Settled debts and throwaway goods are mused on together.
explanation.definitionFit: Diaper is the American word for a nappy, and nowadays most are single-use disposables.

clue.text: Rare arachnids pet maybe found in faeces one overturned

indicators.note: something found in another is inside it, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: everyday word for faeces
a dog is an example of a pet

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, which in a down entry reads backwards

parts.note: an means one

explanation.surface: Uncommon spiders turn up in a pet's droppings.
explanation.walkthrough: Rare looks like part of the definition's description, and it is: these arachnids are seldom seen as well as being an obscure name.
explanation.definitionFit: Podogona is an old name for the Ricinulei, a small rarely seen order of arachnids.

clue.text: We were devoted to manes — deduce odd ones from image

parts.note: to infer is to deduce

indicators.note: the odd ones are the letters in first, third and fifth places of the following word

parts.note: its first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a horse-lover's devotion while working something out from a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: Manes are not horses' hair but the Roman spirits of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferiae were the offerings Romans made to the manes, the deified souls of dead ancestors, so they were dedicated to them.

clue.text: Lure for angler in Dee, age about five

parts.note: dee is the spoken name of the letter D

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word wraps around a numeral

parts.note: an eon is an age
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: An angler fishing the river Dee has used the same lure for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a famous salmon river, but here it is just the letter's name. D then E(V)ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A devon, or devon minnow, is a spinning artificial bait used by anglers for salmon and trout.

clue.text: Countryman's shaft, one inserted in slab

indicators.note: inserted in means put inside, so one letter goes within the word

parts.note: a stele is an upright stone slab bearing an inscription
a means one

explanation.surface: A farmer fixes a handle into a stone block.
explanation.walkthrough: Countryman's flags a dialect word. A goes into STELE: STE(A)LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Steale is a dialect word for a handle or long shaft, such as that of a tool.

clue.text: Moths can end up on clothes finally

parts.note: a can is a tin

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to end is to die, read upwards

indicators.note: finally picks out just the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: Moths are able to finish up on garments in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Can looks like a verb but is the noun TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tineids are moths of the family Tineidae, which includes the clothes moths whose larvae eat fabric.

clue.text: What even the best have occasionally, not on time

definitions.text: What even the best have occasionally

parts.note: off is the opposite of on
a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: Even top performers sometimes fail to keep time.
explanation.definitionFit: An off day is a day of below-par performance, something even the finest performers suffer now and then.

clue.text: Ball missed by keeper often goes this, once past

definitions.text: Ball missed by keeper often goes this
definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket a ball the wicketkeeper misses often goes '...', an extra run
second meaning: an old word for past or beyond

explanation.surface: A cricket ball that gets past the keeper runs on for extras.
explanation.walkthrough: A bye in cricket is a run scored when the ball beats the batsman and the wicketkeeper; the ball goes FOR BYE. Once flags an archaic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Forbye is an old and Scots word meaning past, beside or besides, and split in two it describes a ball that goes for a bye.

clue.text: As Med's stormy, I put in, leaving open waters

indicators.note: put in means inserted, so the letter goes inside the others
stormy means tossed about, so the letters are churned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written; the 's is is
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor puts into port because the Mediterranean is rough, avoiding the open sea.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside the rearranged letters MDSEA: M(I)DSEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Midsea means the middle of the sea, far from land, which is the open water.

clue.text: Model of Austin, first scrapped, like former brands?

indicators.note: a model of something is a new version of it, so the letters are remodelled
the first letter is scrapped, thrown away, from the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A car fan asks whether an old Austin model counts as a vanished brand.
explanation.walkthrough: Brands looks like car makes such as Austin, a defunct British car marque, but means marks burnt into skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Inust is an obsolete word for burnt in, as a brand is burned into the hide, hence former.

clue.text: What text critics argue over like veteran campaigners? Mostly

indicators.note: mostly means all but a little, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: old soldiers carry scars from their campaigns

explanation.surface: Scholars squabble over a passage about battle-hardened old soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: SCARRED loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarre is a crux in Shakespeare's All's Well That Ends Well, a word whose meaning editors have long disputed.

clue.text: Fish o' the sea, inclusive set numerically

parts.note: a cod is a fish
the shortened of, taken as written
the main is a poetic word for the open sea

explanation.surface: A fish from the sea is described in an old shanty-like phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics the codomain is the set containing every possible output value of a function, including its actual range.

clue.text: Does it indicate hesitations, a negative quality?

parts.note: surface reading: a question about the signs of a halting speaker
setter's reading: the answer split into three short words is an instruction, a letter in a two-letter word, which builds a word for hesitations

explanation.surface: A speaker wonders whether all those ums and ers count against them.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read MINUS as M IN US, and putting M inside US makes UMS, which are hesitations. Literally, a minus is a drawback.
explanation.definitionFit: A minus is a drawback or disadvantage, the opposite of a plus, so it is a negative quality.

clue.text: Aims when going after fish

indicators.note: going after places one piece behind the other in reading order

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: Someone states their goals while hunting fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas can mean intentions or plans, as in 'the idea is to win', so they are aims.

clue.text: Churchill's trademark time? In retrospect disastrous

indicators.note: in retrospect means looking back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: Winston Churchill was rarely seen without a cigar
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A historian reflects that Churchill's characteristic moment proved a calamity.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic means causing great suffering or destruction, close in sense to catastrophic.

clue.text: Put down in a bed for Marie Antoinette?

parts.note: taken as written
lit is French for bed, and Marie Antoinette was French

explanation.surface: Royalty is laid to rest in a French queen's bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Alit is a past tense of alight, so a bird that alit has settled or landed, put down.

clue.text: Sweet-smelling wood adored for carving

indicators.note: carving cuts something into a new shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woodcarver loves a fragrant timber for working.
explanation.definitionFit: The deodar is a Himalayan cedar whose aromatic timber is prized for building and carving.

clue.text: Old boy yearns for figures without curves!

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
to long is to yearn

explanation.surface: A former pupil pines for shapely women, or rather the lack of them.
explanation.walkthrough: Figures without curves sounds like a joke about bodies, but means straight-sided shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblongs are rectangles, geometric shapes with straight sides and right angles and no rounded edges.

clue.text: Old clothes rare ruler has not (briefly) trimmed

indicators.note: trimmed means cut back, and has not in shortened form names the bit that is cut from the end

parts.note: gerent is a rare word for a ruler or manager

explanation.surface: A rare monarch's old wardrobe has gone untrimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: Not, briefly, is the contraction n't, so NT is cut from the end of GERENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Gere is an obsolete spelling of gear, which once meant apparel or dress, hence old clothes.

clue.text: Born a royal prince, heading for retirement?

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for born
Prince Edward is a son of Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: A prince by birth is about to retire from public life.
explanation.walkthrough: Retirement here is going to bed for the night, not leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedward means towards bed, the direction of someone retiring for the night.

clue.text: Moved to a new disposition? As teams' diets will be

indicators.note: what the letters will be is the definition itself, rearranged into a new disposition

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sports teams' eating regimes are being reorganised.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition doubles as the anagram signal: the letters of AS TEAMS DIETS will be moved to a new arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Metastasised means spread to a new site in the body, as a cancer does, a medical sense of relocation.
